Sir Arthur Cotton constructed the Dowleswaram Anicut.
The Dowleswaram Anicut was completed in 1852.
Chalukya Bhima I built the Bhimeshwara Temple on the banks of the Godavari.
Chalukya Bhima I built the twin temples of Draksharama Bhimeswara and Kumararama Bhimeswara.
Kumararama Bhimeswara is located at Samalkota.
Recharla Rudra built the Ramappa Temple at Palampet.
Rudra Deva built the Thousand-Pillar Temple at Anumakonda.
Rudra built the Pakala Tank.
Rudra was an army officer of Ganapathi Deva.
The Pakala Tank was built across the Munneru river basin in Warangal.
The Satavahana queens built chaityams for Buddhist monks.
Prola Raju II built the Swayambhu Devalayam.
Prola Raju II built Kesavala.
The Swayambhu Devalayam is dedicated to Lord Shiva.
Kesavala is dedicated to Lord Shiva.
Betha Raju II built Setti Samudram.
Betha Raju II built Kete Samudram.
Betha Raju II built Kesari Samudram.
Kesari Samudram was named after Betha Raju II's royal title, Vikrama Kesari.
Prolaya Vema Reddy built the steps to Pathala Ganga at Srisailam and Ahobilam.
Prolaya Vema Reddy built stepped stone pathways called Sopanamargas.
The Sopanamargas made pilgrimage to the Ahobilam shrines easier.
The Sopanamargas made the perilous descent to Pathala Ganga at the Srisailam Mallikarjuna temple easier.
Anavema Reddy built the Veera Siro Mandapam at Srisailam.
The Veera Siro Mandapam was for Shaivite devotees.
Shaivite devotees offered their own limbs or heads through Siro-karthanam to Lord Mallikarjuna.
Mailamma built the Jaina Basthi at Anamakonda.
Mailamma was the wife of Bethanamathya.

10.text: Satavahana Amatyas administered the Aharas.
Satavahana Mahasenadhipathulu were military officers who administered Aharas away from the capital.
Satavahana Visvamaatyulu, Rajaamatyulu, and Mahaamatyulu were employees who helped in administration.
Satavahana Visvamaatyulu were consulted for important decisions.
Satavahana Rajaamatyulu were advisors.
Satavahana Mahaamatyulu were special officers.
The Satavahana Mantri Parishad helped the king in administration.
The Satavahana Nigama Sabha, or Nigama Subhas, looked after the administration of cities and towns.
The Satavahana Gramani had jurisdiction over five or ten villages.
The Satavahana Gaaha Pati was a Karshaka Pratinidhi, or representative of farmers.
The Kakatiya Bahathara Viyog was the collective name of all administration departments.
The Kakatiya Bahathara Viyogaduipathi held supreme authority over all departments.
Kakatiya Ayagarlu were officials who enjoyed land without any cess or tax.
The number of Kakatiya Ayagarlu was twelve.
Kakatiya Pedakapu was also known as Reddy.
The Kakatiya Pedakapu, or Reddy, levied taxes based on the assessment given by the Karanam.
The number of Kakatiya village officers was twelve.
The ancient and medieval Pradvivaka was an advisor to the king in judiciary.
Reddy Srinatha served as an educational officer in the court of Pedakomati Vema Reddy.
The Collector’s administration came into existence in place of the Board of Revenue in 1794.
The Office of Collector was introduced in the North Sarkar region in 1802.
G. N. Taylor was the Sub-Collector of Rajahmundry.
G. N. Taylor opened Anglo-vernacular schools.
V. Veeranna was an Andhra officer who helped Sir Arthur Cotton in the construction of the Godavari Barrage.
